history.period: CONFLICT (verify): 1942 per myadhyatm vs built 1975 CE per inheritage.foundation
history.summary: CONFLICT OF SOURCES - two web accounts of the Wokha Shiv Mandir disagree and may describe different shrines conflated under one name: (a) inheritage.foundation places it on DC Hill, built 1975 CE by local Naga tribespeople, with a saffron concrete shikhara and entrance pillars fusing Naga warrior motifs with Hindu iconography; (b) myadhyatm.com calls it the oldest Shiv temple of Nagaland (100+ years), inside the Assam Rifles camp (public access via the eastern gate), centred on a spherical swayambhu Shivlingam spotted in 1942 by a Bihar mason, with a sacred well whose water level never varies, maintained by Assam Rifles; founding members Mr Jivanmal Sharma and Mrs Kamla Devi. Google place data puts a 'Shiv Mandir' on the Kohima-Mokokchung road (26.092342, 94.256174), matching the geocoded result. Do not merge the 1942 and 1975 accounts without verification.

name: Wokha Shiv Mandir
town_description: Wokha is the headquarters of Wokha district in central Nagaland, about 80 km north of Kohima, in Lotha Naga country. It is famous for the Doyang river valley, the seasonal roosting of Amur falcons at the Doyang reservoir from October to November, and views of Mount Tiyi. The town serves as a modest district administrative centre surrounded by hills.

travel.road: On the Kohima-Mokokchung road in Wokha town; one account places it inside the Assam Rifles camp with access via the camp gate (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; October-November for Amur falcons at Doyang (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:07 AM to 7:15 PM per an Instagram place listing (verify).
